pool.prompt: What is the minimum hi-vis apparel class for a roadway flagger during daytime work in a MUTCD temporary traffic control zone?
choices: Class 1 — minimum background material
Class 2 — ANSI/ISEA 107 roadway minimum
Class 3 — required only at night
No class standard — any bright-colored vest is acceptable
pool.explanation: ANSI/ISEA 107 Class 2 is the minimum for daytime roadway work in a temporary traffic control zone. Class 3 is required for nighttime or high-speed (>50 mph) zones; Class 1 is for off-road, low-traffic environments.

pool.prompt: Per MUTCD Chapter 6E, which device must flaggers use to control traffic?
choices: A hand flag (standard traffic flag)
A STOP/SLOW paddle (octagonal, STOP on one face, SLOW on the reverse)
Either a flag or a paddle — the flagger's choice
A lighted wand at night, flag during the day
pool.explanation: MUTCD Chapter 6E specifies the STOP/SLOW paddle as the required device for flaggers. A hand flag alone is not compliant — the paddle is more visible and less ambiguous. STOP is red with white letters; SLOW is orange with black letters.

pool.prompt: Which section of a MUTCD temporary traffic control zone is the empty space between the end of the taper and the closest worker or equipment in the activity area?
choices: Advance warning area
Transition area
Buffer space (longitudinal)
Termination area
pool.explanation: The longitudinal buffer space serves as a vehicle-recovery zone: if a driver exits the lane at the taper, the buffer is the distance before they reach the crew. Buffer length scales with approach speed.

pool.prompt: The MUTCD is published by which federal agency?
choices: OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Administration)
FHWA (Federal Highway Administration)
NHTSA (National Highway Traffic Safety Administration)
FCC (Federal Communications Commission)
pool.explanation: The Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), part of US DOT, publishes the MUTCD. States adopt the MUTCD as a condition of receiving federal highway funding, making it effectively the national standard for work zone traffic control.

pool.prompt: What is the correct order in which a work zone's temporary traffic control components should be REMOVED at the end of a job?
choices: Advance warning signs first, then termination-area cones, then taper cones, then activity-area cones
Confirm activity area clear -> remove activity-area cones toward the taper -> remove taper cones -> remove termination-area cones -> remove advance warning signs
Remove all cones and signs simultaneously regardless of order
Remove advance warning signs, taper, and activity-area cones simultaneously, then termination cones last
pool.explanation: Removing termination devices LAST — after the activity area is clear — protects the workers still in the zone. Driving through the termination area before the work space is cleared creates a struck-by hazard for the remaining crew.
pool.citation: MUTCD 11th Edition (2023), Part 6, Chapter 6B — General Requirements.

pool.prompt: What are the five components of a MUTCD temporary traffic control (TTC) zone, in order from a driver's approach?
choices: Buffer, Transition, Advance Warning, Activity, Termination
Advance Warning, Transition, Activity, Buffer, Termination
Termination, Activity, Buffer, Transition, Advance Warning
Advance Warning, Buffer, Activity, Transition, Termination
pool.explanation: A TTC zone consists of: Advance Warning Area (alerts approaching drivers), Transition Area (channelizes traffic via a taper), Buffer Space (vehicle-recovery zone with no work permitted), Activity Area (the actual work space), and Termination Area (where traffic returns to normal).

pool.prompt: What does OSHA/MUTCD guidance say about workers exposed to traffic or construction equipment within the right-of-way, regarding hi-vis apparel — does elevation in a bucket truck change the requirement?
choices: Elevated workers are exempt from hi-vis requirements since they're not directly in the traffic lane
All workers within the right-of-way exposed to traffic or equipment must wear hi-vis meeting Class 2 or 3 — elevation does not remove the struck-by exposure or the requirement
Hi-vis is only required for the flagger, not other crew members
Hi-vis requirements apply only to nighttime work regardless of elevation
pool.explanation: MUTCD/ANSI requirements apply based on proximity to a traffic lane and right-of-way exposure, not physical elevation. A worker in a bucket truck adjacent to a live lane is still exposed to the struck-by hazard from an errant vehicle and must wear the appropriate hi-vis class.

pool.prompt: Match each traffic control device or role to its correct description.

items.label: Octagonal device: STOP on one face, SLOW on the reverse
Channelizes traffic out of the closed lane
Empty recovery zone with no work permitted
Where traffic returns to its normal path

pool.explanation: Each element of MUTCD Part 6 traffic control serves a distinct role: the STOP/SLOW paddle directs traffic at a flagger station; the transition area's taper merges traffic out of a lane; the buffer space is a deliberately empty recovery zone; and the termination area returns traffic to normal flow.
